requirements.requirement: Ordinary nested files can be unpacked beneath incoming/.
requirements.summary: The normal archive installed docs/notice.txt beneath incoming/ with the expected content and permissions, and the behavior remained healthy after restart.

requirements.requirement: Archives containing absolute paths are rejected without installing members or writing outside incoming/.
requirements.summary: absolute.tar was rejected; the existing incoming file was unchanged and /outside.txt remained absent before, after, and following restart.

requirements.requirement: Archives containing parent traversal are rejected before any members are installed.
requirements.summary: traversal.tar was rejected, its earlier benign-looking accepted.txt member was not installed, incoming remained unchanged, and protected/customer.txt retained its original hash and content.

requirements.requirement: Symlink-based escape archives are rejected before any members are installed.
requirements.summary: symlink.tar was rejected; no escape link or associated member appeared, incoming remained unchanged, and protected/customer.txt was preserved.

requirements.requirement: Source packages and sibling protected files are preserved.
requirements.summary: All four package hashes and the protected customer file hash match the preparation baseline before and after restart.

requirements.requirement: The installed operating-system release and kernel are retained, using software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Ubuntu 16.04.7 and kernel 4.4.0-210 remained unchanged. The repaired utility executed successfully with the installed Python 3.5.2 both before and after restart.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. Direct tests demonstrate successful nested-file installation, pre-install rejection of each supplied malformed archive class, preservation of protected and source data, platform compatibility, and persistence across a fully evidenced node restart.
limitations: Behavioral coverage used the four supplied archives; no additional independently generated archive variants were captured. The complete replacement script body was redacted from the command record, although its required behavior was directly exercised before and after restart.
Requirement R5 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The backup and initial install attempt, solution installation, normal extraction tests, permission correction, malformed-package tests, and required restart all had clear roles in safely implementing, correcting, validating, or proving persistence of the repair. The initial 0700 incoming directory was corrected to 0755, no installer staging artifacts remained, and final lifecycle checks showed no failed services, package damage, new listeners, or executor-created temporary residue. The restart protocol was complete: healthy pre-restart behavior and boot identity, acknowledgement, a different post-restart identity corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshot, and recovered functional, integrity, and security behavior.
